daily_thesis: The 2026-08-18 batch makes robot intelligence less about bigger backbones and more about runtime evidence control: VLAs expose process rewards, tactile residuals, counterfactual recovery, stop-aware chunking, and test-time search; Gaussian and LiDAR maps become task-conditioned memories that decide what to update, relight, ignore, or discard; and benchmarks increasingly ask whether the physical evidence path behind a score survives real deployment constraints.

clusters.cluster: VLA control shifts from policy output to runtime repair, residuals, and stop authority
clusters.why: Existing VLA evaluation often waits for terminal success, but this group exposes the intermediate authority that should alter execution. CoRe imagines recovery before physical trial, ViTaR bounds tactile correction as a residual, Robo-Dopamine 2.0 scores process history, SparkVLA ranks stop versus action prefixes, tau0-VLA allocates extra computation to hard subtask choices, and StructRL preserves structured exploration through denoising.
clusters.confidence_note: Six Robot Learning papers independently target VLA recovery, contact, reward, stopping, search, and exploration interfaces.
clusters.lab_action: Run the same LIBERO/RoboCasa-style perturbation tasks with mid-episode goal changes, object displacement, and contact loss, then compare counterfactual recovery, tactile residual authority, process-reward ranking, stop-prefix choice, and test-time search by warning lead time, action delta, and final success.

frontier_memory.body: August 18 strengthens the same commitment-before-action axis with tactile residual authority, counterfactual recovery, stop-aware action chunks, task-driven Gaussian memory, and multi-camera evidence selection.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent geometry notes focused on map quality, localization, and event or LiDAR efficiency.
frontier_memory.body: Today adds a sharper map-governance question: when should a Gaussian or LiDAR map allocate density, relight, reject blur, remember task objects, or stop updating?

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: Prior RI editions repeatedly called for robot-usable geometry and safety diagnostics.
frontier_memory.body: The current batch still lacks one shared benchmark that joins contact residuals, map update choices, multi-view evidence, and recovery authority inside the same closed-loop robot task.

strategy_board.title: Runtime-authority VLA benchmark
strategy_board.thesis: Measure which runtime interface is allowed to alter, delay, or veto a VLA action under the same perturbation.
strategy_board.one_week: Run two manipulation tasks with object displacement, contact loss, and mid-episode instruction change; compare counterfactual recovery, tactile residuals, process rewards, and stop-aware chunking.
strategy_board.four_week: Build a reusable harness that swaps recovery, residual, reward, stop, and test-time search modules around the same frozen VLA backbone.
strategy_board.success: At least one interface predicts or prevents a failure earlier than terminal success while preserving non-perturbed success.
strategy_board.stop: All interfaces rank episodes the same way as final success and cannot identify which next action should change.
strategy_board.asset: Perturbation suite, action deltas, contact states, recovery proposals, reward curves, stop-prefix choices, and veto outcomes.

strategy_board.title: Task-driven Gaussian map governance
strategy_board.thesis: Turn Gaussian and LiDAR mapping from passive reconstruction into a policy for update, relight, reject, remember, and discard decisions.
strategy_board.one_week: Create a small scene set with dynamic lighting, camera motion blur, distractor objects, LiDAR degeneracy, and task-relevant occlusions.
strategy_board.four_week: Compare SpotlessGS-style relighting, event-modulated blur modeling, geometry-aware density control, task-driven memory, and hybrid ICP under identical robot tasks.
strategy_board.success: A map-update policy improves localization or manipulation recovery under at least two degradation families without increasing false stable memories.
strategy_board.stop: Map governance only improves visual metrics and does not change downstream robot decisions.
strategy_board.asset: Degraded multi-view scenes, event/LiDAR streams, Gaussian update traces, task object masks, and downstream action outcomes.

strategy_board.title: Physical-evidence benchmark provenance
strategy_board.thesis: Make every score identify the camera, modality, scenario field, resource budget, or trust boundary that supports the deployment claim.
strategy_board.one_week: Choose one flood-response, driving, or indoor navigation task and mark which view, modality, scenario variable, and edge budget is decisive for action.
strategy_board.four_week: Evaluate VLM segmentation, cross-view reasoning, scenario characterization, timely BEV perception, and embodied-agent attacks using the same provenance schema.
strategy_board.success: The provenance schema exposes a model ranking reversal or a safety failure hidden by the aggregate score.
strategy_board.stop: The provenance fields do not predict action errors beyond ordinary held-out accuracy.
strategy_board.asset: Scenario cards, view-authority labels, modality-degradation cases, edge-budget traces, trust-boundary attacks, and action-impact annotations.
